_readme: A22 — THE SHOE BRAND'S LOGISTICS REGISTRIES: who carries the parcels, and where a buyer can fetch one.
★ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL. The admin has carried `/logistics/carriers` and `/logistics/pickup-points`
since the L3/L4 waves, and on this box both screens were EMPTY — measured 2026-09-04 against the running
kernel: `carrier` 0 rows and `pickup_location` 0 rows in the shoe tenant. An empty screen teaches nothing
about a capability; worse, it reads as a capability that does not work. Same argument that made the
`chrome` app be born configured rather than merely installed.
⚠️ BOTH REGISTRIES ARE TENANT-WIDE, NOT PER STORE — measured against the commands themselves:
`shipping.carrier.create` takes {name, tracking_url_template} and `pickup_location.create` takes an
address, and NEITHER takes a `store_id`. So everything here belongs to the brand, and both the Forge
storefront and the Outlet see it. `seed/totem.json` writes up the same limitation for the counter's own
point, one tenant away.
⛔ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT WOULD HAVE CHANGED THE SHOP: no
`shipping.method.create` of kind `pickup`. A point is only REACHABLE from a checkout when a pickup METHOD
with a rate covering the destination exists, so what this file produces is a populated admin registry and
not a new checkout option. That is exactly what A22 asked for, and adding the method would have done two
things nobody asked for: put a «Retirar na loja» option into the Forge and Outlet funnels, and FLIP the
live proof order in both shops from delivery to pickup (`seed/commerce.mjs` prefers a usable pickup option
over a delivery one, by intention, and says so).
📌 The card `SEED-PICKUP-SO-METADE` is the other half of the same subject — «a história semeada produz
encomenda ESPERANDO no balcão e nunca uma RETIRADA». Reaching these points from a checkout and seeding a
collected order belong together, in that card, not scattered across two slices.
★ THE TRACKING TEMPLATES ARE CHECKED BY THE KERNEL, not by taste: `{code}` has to appear EXACTLY ONCE
(`assertTrackingTemplate`, packages/core/src/commands/shipping.ts), because a template with none produces
a link to the carrier's home page for every parcel in the store — which looks like it works.

carriers.name: Correios
carriers.why: The one every Brazilian shop has. It is first in the list because a demo is read top-down and the first row should be the row a visitor recognises.

carriers.name: Jadlog
carriers.why: The private courier a mid-sized brand actually contracts beside the Correios — which is the point of the registry having more than one row: `shipment.carrier` was free text until L3, and the same company was spelled three ways.

carriers.name: Loggi
carriers.why: Last-mile in the capitals. Third row, so the screen shows a LIST rather than a pair, and so a merchant reading it sees that the registry is theirs to grow.

carriers.name: Retirada na loja
carriers.why: ★ THE ROW THAT PROVES THE TEMPLATE IS OPTIONAL. `tracking_url_template` is nullable on both create and update, with the meaning «this carrier publishes no tracking page» — and a parcel the buyer fetches has nothing to track. Without a row like this the screen would suggest that a carrier without a link is a carrier badly registered.

pickup_points.name: Forge Loja Oscar Freire
pickup_points.instructions: Retire no caixa da loja com um documento com foto. Pedidos ficam disponíveis por 7 dias.

pickup_points.name: Forge Shopping Morumbi
pickup_points.instructions: Balcão de retirada ao lado da entrada do estacionamento G2.

pickup_points.name: Forge Outlet Ipanema
pickup_points.instructions: Retirada no primeiro andar. Traga o número do pedido.

pickup_points.name: Forge Centro de Distribuição Extrema
pickup_points.instructions: Retirada apenas com agendamento prévio, de segunda a sexta.

_hours_why: THE WEEK IS THE KERNEL'S OWN VOCABULARY AND IT IS STRICT. `pickupHoursSchema` is `.strict()` over
`mon..sun` (packages/core/src/shipping/pickup.ts): a file that wrote `seg` would be REFUSED rather than
stored as a shop closed every day, which is the failure the strictness exists to prevent.
A `null` day is closed; an omitted day is closed too — the two spellings mean the same thing, and every
point here writes all seven so the file reads as a week rather than as a set of exceptions.
⚠️ AN OVERNIGHT SHIFT IS REFUSED BY THE KERNEL (`open < close`), so none is written. That is the
kernel's deliberate cut, not a gap in this file.
⛔ NO COORDINATES. `lat`/`lng` are optional and they are DATA a merchant pastes from a map service;
inventing plausible ones for four addresses would be inventing facts about real streets. A point with
none is fully usable — it simply never sorts by proximity, which is what the storefront degrades to
anyway when the shopper declines geolocation.
